summary: Stefan Anacker worked in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison between circa 1965 and 1970, studying under Alex Wayman.

Stefan Baums is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who completed his dissertation at the University of Washington (circa 2002–2009). He held posts at the University of Copenhagen, the University of Washington, the Bavarian Academy of Sciences, and the University of Munich.

Stefan Larsson specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Stockholm under Per-Arne Berglie and Erik af Edholm, and held posts at the University of Virginia, UC Berkeley, and the University of Gävle.

Stefan Mario Maul is a historian, archaeologist, and linguist. After studying at the University of Göttingen and the Free University of Berlin, he became Ordinarius for Assyriology at Heidelberg University in 1995 and led a research unit at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences.

Stefania Travagnin is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She served as an assistant professor and centre director at the University of Groningen from circa 2013 to 2020 before joining SOAS University of London around 2020.

Stefano Zacchetti was a Buddhist studies scholar and Sinologist educated at Ca' Foscari University, Sichuan University, and Leiden University. He held academic posts at Padua, Soka University, Ca' Foscari, UC Berkeley, and as Yehan Numata Professor at the University of Oxford.

Steffen Döll specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. After completing his degrees at the University of Munich and studying at Kyoto University, he held posts at Munich, Seikei University, and the University of Hamburg, where he became Numata Professor in 2015.

Stella Kramrisch was an art historian and Indologist who earned her doctorate at the University of Vienna under Max Dvořák and Josef Strzygowski. She held appointments at Visva-Bharati, Calcutta, the Courtauld Institute, the University of Pennsylvania, and the Philadelphia Museum of Art.

Sten Konow was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who earned his doctorate at Halle-Wittenberg under Richard Pischel. He served as Government Epigraphist for India and held professorships at the universities of Oslo and Hamburg.

Stephan Kigensan Licha is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who completed his PhD at SOAS University of London by 2012. He subsequently held postdoctoral positions at Waseda University and the University of Tokyo.

Stephan Marcus Salzberg is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of British Columbia, attested in 1983, under teachers Yoshitaka Iriya, Shoko Kanaoka, and Daniel L. Overmyer.

Stephan V. Beyer is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at the University of Rochester and under Richard Hugh Robinson. He served as a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from circa 1972 to 1979 and worked at Sidley Austin.

Stephanie Kaza is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Oberlin, Stanford, UC Santa Cruz (PhD), and Starr King School for the Ministry. She served as professor at the University of Vermont (1991–2015) and president of the Society for Buddhist-Christian Studies.
Stephanie Roemer is a scholar in the field of Tibetology who conducted her doctoral studies under supervisors Eberhard Sandschneider and Toni Huber.

Stephanie W. Jamison is an Indologist and linguist who completed her doctorate at Yale under Stanley Insler and Warren Cowgill. She held posts at Harvard University and later became Professor of Sanskrit and Indo-Iranian Linguistics at UCLA.

Stephen Addiss was a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history who earned his PhD from the University of Michigan. He served as professor of art history at the University of Kansas (1977–1992) and Tucker-Boatwright Professor at the University of Richmond (1992–2013).

Stephen Batchelor is an author and scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who trained under various traditional teachers at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, Rikon, and Songgwangsa. He led Sharpham College (circa 1992–2000) and later joined Bodhi College.

Stephen C. Berkwitz specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He conducted research at the University of Kelaniya and the University of Colombo, and held appointments at Missouri State University and Ruhr University Bochum.

Stephen F. Teiser is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. After earning his doctorate at Princeton University, he taught at Middlebury College before returning to Princeton, where he became D. T. Suzuki Professor in Buddhist Studies.

Stephen Fuchs was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Vienna under Wilhelm Schmidt. He taught at St. Xavier's College in Mumbai, founded the Anthropos Institute and the Institute of Indian Culture, and visited San Carlos.
